content:
The owner of the small Bichon Frise named Weiwei, who was killed by a dog, posted a tribute on social media today. The owner said Weiwei loved going out and took two walks every day. Yesterday, while walking at the pet park, a large dog nearly half a person's height suddenly rushed out and bit Weiwei on the neck.

The owner recounted trying various methods, including kicking the large dog, spraying water at its nose, and using treats to distract it, but the large dog held onto Weiwei and refused to let go. The owner said: "I screamed for help and am grateful to the kind passers-by who assisted, but faced with a large dog weighing dozens of pounds that refused to let go, no one could do anything. I could only watch helplessly as my little dog lost her life."

Weiwei died on the spot. The owner recounted that the large dog remained guarding Weiwei's body until police arrived and restrained it, after which the owner was finally able to collect the remains. "I later learned that the vicious dog had also killed another small dog. From beginning to end, the owner of the large dog never appeared."

The owner said the family is in deep pain over the sudden tragedy and has been unable to sleep through the night. "Weiwei was an especially well-behaved and gentle little dog, a little angel to our entire family. I miss holding her and kissing her so much. I cannot believe she has suddenly left us like this." The owner uploaded the last video of Weiwei before the incident, showing her sitting in a stroller at a shopping mall, looking obedient and adorable. The owner said: "Only by repeatedly watching her curious and lovely expression can I temporarily erase the terrifying image from my mind."

The Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) replied to media enquiries yesterday, stating that after examination, the dog involved in the killing has a microchip and a valid dog licence. The department will contact the dog's owner using the information on the licence and will investigate the incident. If there is sufficient evidence, prosecution will be initiated.

The AFCD stated that dog owners must always keep their dogs under proper control, including securely leashing large dogs, to prevent causing nuisance or harm to other people or animals. According to the Rabies Ordinance, dogs must be leashed or otherwise properly controlled when in public places, or in other places where it can reasonably be expected that the dog may wander into public places. Offenders may be fined HK$10,000.

The Collective is enquiring with the AFCD whether the dog owner has been contacted today, and is awaiting a reply.
